title: Abelian etale sheaves on a finite clopen coproduct decompose componentwise
statement: Let $C=\coprod_{i\in I}C_i$ be a finite coproduct of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with coprojections $\iota_i:C_i\hookrightarrow C$ open and closed. Restriction along the $\iota_i$ identifies the category of abelian sheaves on $C_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] with the finite product of the categories of abelian sheaves on $(C_i)_{\mathrm{Et}}$: a sheaf $F$ is recovered from the family $(\iota_i^{-1}F)_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and morphisms are recovered componentwise. Under this identification, the global-sections functor $F\mapsto F(C)$ is the finite product of the component global-sections functors $G_i\mapsto G_i(C_i)$.

source.place: first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 0A5B (etale-cohomology-lemma-constant-smooth-statements), finite disjoint-union decomposition

proof.text: For an object U \to C of C_Et put U_i = U x_C C_i. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the U_i are pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering U, so {U_i \to U}_i is a covering of C_Et and U_i x_U U_j is empty for i != j. The equalizer sheaf condition in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], together with F(empty)=0 obtained from the empty covering of the empty scheme, therefore gives a natural isomorphism F(U) ~= product_i F(U_i).

source.place: Lemma 0A5B proof, first paragraph, finite disjoint-union decomposition

proof.text: For each i, the localized site C_Et/C_i is equivalent to (C_i)_Et by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open]. The restriction theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies the inverse-image sheaf iota_i^{-1}F evaluated on U_i with F(U_i), naturally in U and F. Thus the preceding decomposition identifies F(U) with product_i (iota_i^{-1}F)(U_i).

source.place: Section 00XZ, localization of the etale site and inverse-image restriction

proof.text: Conversely, for a family (G_i)_i with G_i in Ab((C_i)_Et), define G on C_Et by G(U)=product_i G_i(U x_C C_i), with restriction maps induced by base change. The decomposition in step 1 shows that G satisfies the sheaf equalizer condition. The same componentwise formula gives natural isomorphisms from each G_i to the restriction of G and from F to the sheaf reconstructed from its restrictions; hence restriction and this construction are quasi-inverse functors.

source.place: Lemma 0A5B proof, first paragraph, finite-product assembly

proof.text: A morphism between two sheaves is determined by its components on the U_i because the isomorphism of step 1 is natural; conversely, a family of component morphisms defines a morphism by the product formula. Taking U=C in step 2 gives F(C) ~= product_i (iota_i^{-1}F)(C_i), which is the asserted global-sections identification.
